title: Unified storage: service token lacking delegated permission must fail loudly, not return empty results
answers: Why does a label-selector LIST return an empty list with HTTP 200 even though the resources exist?
search-api is denying every hit for storage-api but there's no error or metric
How to tell a deployment mistake (missing delegated token permission) from a legitimate access denial
body:
Symptom: a LIST/Check/BatchCheck on behalf of a user silently returns zero/denied results (HTTP 200, empty list) with no error, log, or metric; only a trace shows check_count=1, authz_check_count=0.
Root cause: authlib's authz.CheckServicePermissions (authz/service_permissions.go) denies the check itself when the caller's token has no delegated permission for that group/resource/verb, so the authz service is never even asked - that path is indistinguishable from an ordinary denial.
Fix pattern: before forwarding to the underlying client, call serviceCanDelegate(ctx, id, group, resource, verb) in pkg/storage/unified/resource/access.go:authzLimitedClient; if the identity carries some token permissions but not this one, return ErrServiceCannotDelegate (wrapping the missing permission string), log at error level, and increment grafana_grpc_authz_limited_client_missing_delegated_permission_total{group,resource,verb}.
Constraints: identities with no token permissions at all (len(id.GetTokenPermissions())==0 && len(id.GetTokenDelegatedPermissions())==0 - typical of single-tenant/in-process callers) must be skipped; only a token that carries some permissions but not the specific one being used is treated as a deployment mistake.
applies: pkg/storage/unified/resource access-check layer (authzLimitedClient) for any Check/Compile/BatchCheck path that delegates on behalf of a user
says: The resource list displays zero items without showing any permission warning or error.
Display an explicit access error when a service token lacks delegation privileges.
Saved dashboard resources vanish from the search screen even though user permissions exist.
The system must alert administrators if token delegation fails instead of pretending nothing exists.
Filtering items by label shows a blank table rather than reporting an authorization problem.
